# payroll/

South African payroll: PAYE, UIF, SDL, ETI + run lifecycle, leave, termination/IRP5 prep, tax directives, UIF declarations. Pure engines have no DB; DB services are all company-scoped.

## Modules
- **Pure engines (no DB)**: `payrollTypes.ts`, `taxTables.ts` (TAX_2025/2026/2027; `getTaxYearConfig` THROWS `UnsupportedTaxYearError` for any other year; SA tax year ends Feb → March N ⇒ tax year N+1), `payeEngine.ts` (annual→rebates→medical credits→monthly), `payeAnnualPayment.ts` (annual payments, `payeTreatment`), `uifEngine.ts` (1%+1%, capped at ceiling), `sdlEngine.ts` (1% leviable; exempt <= R500 000 annual remuneration), `etiEngine.ts` + `etiTables.ts` (18–29, non-UIF-excluded, ≤24m employed; formula chosen by pay period), `payrollCalculator.ts` (`calculatePayrollLine` orchestrator), `validationEngine.ts`, `irp5ValidationEngine.ts`, `payrollJournalSplitBuilder.ts`.
- **Run lifecycle**: `payrollRunService.ts` (CRUD + `calculatePayrollRun` populates lines), `payrollRunLock.ts` (period lock), `sdlLeviabilityService.ts` (SDL threshold basis), `payrollApprovalService.ts` (`approvePayrollRun` → approved + posts JE), `payrollJournalPostingService.ts` (`postPayrollRunJournal` / `reversePayrollRunJournal`), `payrollBatchService.ts`, `payrollBulkEmployeeService.ts`.
- **Employees + history**: `payrollEmployeeService.ts`, `payrollEmployeeComponentService.ts`, `payrollEmployeeHistoryService.ts`, `payrollComponentService.ts`, `payPackageService.ts`, `payScaleService.ts`, `sarsCodesService.ts`.
- **Leave**: `payrollLeaveService.ts`, `leaveAccrualService.ts` (pure BCEA accrual), `payrollTerminationService.ts`.
- **Statutory**: `uifDeclarationService.ts` (UI-19 + `markUifDeclarationPaid`: DR 2150 / CR 1110), `taxDirectiveService.ts`, `taxDirectivePaymentService.ts` (`applyTaxDirective`: DR 5200 / CR 2140 / CR 1110), `easyFileExportService.ts` (e@syFile EMP501 CSV).
- **Loans / costing**: `payrollLoanService.ts`, `payrollLoanReversal.ts` (undoes a run's own loan payments, tombstoning each on `payroll_loan_payment_reversals`), `payrollRunLoanApplication.ts` (`applyRunLoans` — reverse-then-re-apply in one locked transaction; refuses a run whose `journal_entry_id` is still set, in BOTH directions), `payrollCostAllocationService.ts`, `costCentreGlMappingService.ts`, `costCentreRunSummary.ts` (`costCentreSummaryForRun`: a run rolled up by cost centre, split by allocation; the master itself is `core/costCentreService`), `cashPayRegisterService.ts`.
- **Variance / duplicates / training / equity**: `payrollVarianceService.ts`, `payrollDuplicateDetectionService.ts`, `trainingEventService.ts`, `equityReportService.ts`.
- **Parallel-run comparison (Dotbiz Workstream C)**: `payrollParallelRunTypes.ts`, `payrollExternalCsvParser.ts` (pure; SA number formats → integer cents), `payrollParallelRunComparator.ts` (pure; IsaFlow run vs imported external payslips, per-employee per-component cent diffs), `payrollParallelRunCsv.ts` (pure CSV render), `payrollExternalImportService.ts` (DB; mig 495), `payrollParallelRunReportService.ts` (DB; assembles report).

## Caller contract
Invoked by `withCompany`-wrapped API routes in `pages/api/accounting/payroll/*`. Every DB function takes `companyId` first. Pure engines accept plain typed inputs and return plain results.

## Main function signatures
- `createPayrollRun(companyId, input) / getPayrollRun(companyId, id) / calculatePayrollRun(runId, companyId)`.
- `approvePayrollRun(companyId, runId, userId)` — status `draft|calculated|processed → approved`, posts JE, links `payroll_run_headers.journal_entry_id`. Every refusal (not found, status, any journal-plan blocker via `judgePayrollApproval`) is thrown BEFORE the status write as `PayrollApprovalRefusedError` (its own module, `payrollApprovalRefusal.ts`); callers answer only that as a 4xx and rethrow the rest, so a post-write failure rolls back (K-079). Returns the plan's `advisories`.
- `judgePayrollApproval(companyId, runId)` (`payrollApprovalGate.ts`) — THE approval gate, used by `approvePayrollRun`, `previewPayrollApproval` (`GET /api/payroll/runs/[id]/journal-plan`, and the MCP dry run): status gate (`approvalStatusRefusal`, `payrollApprovalRefusal.ts`) → for a run linking a journal, by what its reversal chain leaves in the ledger (round 5, below): in force → figures must match (`recalculated_after_posting`); out → replaced; unclear → `posted_journal_not_live` → else plan blockers except `run_not_approved`. Returns `{ plan, posted, replaces, blocker, planHash }`. `approvePayrollRun(…, { expectedPlanHash })` locks the header `FOR UPDATE`, then refuses a different hash with `PayrollApprovalConflictError` (route: 409) before any write.
- `postPayrollRunJournal(companyId, runId, userId)` — DR 5200 Labour = gross + (total_uif÷2) + sdl − etiUsed; CR 2140 PAYE = paye − etiUsed; CR 2150 UIF (employee+employer combined); CR 2160 SDL; CR 1110 Bank (net); zero lines dropped. `etiUsed = max(0, min(eti, paye))` (see Business rules).
- `calculatePayrollLine(input): PayrollLineResult` — pure orchestrator.
- `markUifDeclarationPaid(companyId, declarationId, userId)` — idempotent (returns existing row when already paid).
- `applyTaxDirective(companyId, directiveId, input)` — one payment per directive.
- `computeExpectedAccrual(input): number`, `computeCarryOver(balance, maxCarryOver)` — pure leave helpers.
- `parseExternalPayslipCsv(csv): ExternalCsvParseResult` — pure; header aliases (VIP/Sage), comma/semicolon, SA amount formats; integer cents out.
- `compareParallelRun(isaflowLines, externalRows, opts?): ParallelRunComparisonReport` — pure; employee-number matching is trim/case/zero-pad-insensitive (numeric only); `uifTotal` compares vs ee+er sum; only components present in the external data are compared.
- `getParallelRunReport(companyId, importId, runId?)` — resolves the run by the import's period when runId omitted; `run`/`comparison` null when no run exists.

## Business rules
- **ETI in the journal (K-079, Hein 2026-09-26).** ETI offsets PAYE payable and is presented net of labour cost, capped at the run's PAYE: `etiUsed = max(0, min(total_eti, total_paye))` reduces both DR 5200 and CR 2140, so CR 2140 equals `emp201Service`'s `payePayable` (floored at 0; one run per company per period). ETI beyond PAYE is not booked and is reported as the `eti_beyond_paye` advisory; EMP201 carries none forward. Before the fix the labour debit fell by ETI while 2140 carried full PAYE, so every ETI run was unbalanced and could not post. The ETI formula is SARS' two-table schedule in `etiTables.ts` (K-080 closed 2026-10-18, see Recent changes).
- **Payroll journal plan = what the GL will accept (K-079).**
  - The balance check is exact to the cent. The cost-centre labour split ties to the labour debit
    (residual on the largest share), but only the rounding residual (half a cent per line). A
    bigger gap means the lines disagree with the header, and it is refused as `unbalanced`. ETI
    comes off the cost of the employees whose run lines carry it.
  - The GL poster's refusals are plan blockers (`nothing_to_post`, `negative_amount`,
    `closed_period`, `inactive_target_account`).
  - The deactivated-account check covers cost-centre labour accounts, resolved by id. It is not
    an advisory: `postJournalEntry` refuses deactivated accounts.
  - `approvePayrollRun` refuses every blocker before its status write. withAuth COMMITs a 4xx, so
    a refusal after the write stranded runs `approved` with no journal.
  - A run that already carries its journal (reopen keeps `journal_entry_id`) is refused by none of
    them, because re-approval posts nothing and returns that journal.
- Run state: `draft → calculated → processed → approved`. Re-approve is allowed when `status=approved` but journal unposted (2026-04-24 fix).
- JE posting: do NOT include `runId` inside `sourceDocumentId` (2026-04-24 fix — FK is to `documents`).
- Leave accrual INSERTs supply `company_id` for RLS (2026-04-24 fix); EXCLUDED out of scope in RETURNING clause (same-day fix).
- Employee active-check uses `payroll_employees.status`, NOT `is_active` column (2026-04-24 fix).
- **Run population is by end date, not status (audit 2026-10-18 P4).** `calculatePayrollRun` reads `listPayrollRunEmployees(companyId, period)`: every employee whose `end_date` falls in the run's month, whatever their status; active or terminated employees whose `end_date` is after the month (a run recalculated after they left); active employees with no `end_date`. `updatePayrollEmployee` still sets `terminated` on an end date of today or earlier; that no longer hides the leaver's final pay, leave pay-out and notice pay. Nobody whose `start_date` is after the month. Loan instalments are taken only from the run's employees (`RunLoanInput.employeeIds`). Termination pay-outs already paid in another run are not paid again (`payrollTerminationPaidCheck.ts`: `findPaidTerminationRun`, warning `TERMINATION_ALREADY_PAID`), and the approval gate refuses a run still carrying them (`termination_already_paid`, `findTerminationsPaidElsewhere`). "Paid" = approved or paid, or reopened with a linked journal whose chain is not `out` (a reversed journal stays linked, so the link alone is not enough; a linked journal the company cannot read counts as paid). `approvePayrollRun` takes a company-scoped advisory lock (`lockCompanyPayrollApprovals`) before the header lock so two such approvals cannot both pass; a second approver waits up to 5s, then gets the retryable lock-timeout 503. The posted-journal loan guard (`readRunLoanWork`, live and dry run) counts only the run's employees' instalments. `listPayrollEmployees` (active only; `{ includeTerminated }` adds leavers, for the directive form) is the employee list, not the run. Tests: `tests/integration/p4-leaver-in-final-run.int.test.ts`, `p4-leaver-run-edges.int.test.ts`, `p4-termination-approval-gate.int.test.ts`.
- Leave approver is the session user, never a request field (R-135). Every leave write route is `withWriteAccess` (R-136).
- VIP-parity foundations (2026-04-24): SARS codes table, bureau mode, period lock, variance engine.
- Cash-pay register, IRP5 certificate validation, e@syFile EMP501 CSV — SARS compliance export paths.
- `payrollRunLock`: once locked, period rejects new runs and edits.
- **PAYE by SARS source code (audit 2026-10-18 P3).** `payeTreatment` (`payeAnnualPayment.ts`): `3605` = annual payment, taxed by the SARS annual-payment method (G21 2027 p. 32–33: tax(annual equivalent + payment) − tax(annual equivalent), rebates/credits once, whole difference this month); `39xx` = lump sum, never taxed by the tables — only the PAYE on its directive (`EmployeeComponent.directive`), else `LUMP_SUM_WITHOUT_DIRECTIVE` and nil PAYE; anything else periodic (cumulative since G4, below). `PayrollLineResult.payeSplit` = regular / annualPayment / directive; `paye.monthlyPaye` is their sum; `taxableIncome` excludes lump sums. ETI base unchanged (whole gross). **Severance is paid in the run at its directive's figures** (`payrollSeveranceDirective.ts`, `payrollRunTermination.ts`): none approved → left out, `SEVERANCE_AWAITING_DIRECTIVE`; the first later run pays the leaver the severance line alone (`listSeveranceOnlyRunEmployees`: no salary, loans, UIF or SDL); directive ≠ calculated → paid at the directive, `SEVERANCE_DIRECTIVE_MISMATCH`; paid elsewhere → `SEVERANCE_PAID_BY_DIRECTIVE`. The run claims the directive AT APPROVAL in its one `tax_directive_payments` row (`payroll_run_id`, migration 901, no journal of its own; `payrollRunDirectiveClaim.ts`), so calculate/recalculate never consumes it, a reopened run keeps its claim, re-approval refreshes or releases it, and the stand-alone `applyTaxDirective` answers 409. Gate blockers `severance_directive_unavailable` (directive paid elsewhere, cancelled, or edited since calculation) and `lump_sum_without_directive` (a taxable 39xx component with no directive: no PAYE was deducted, and para 9(3) requires the directive before payment). The claim is taken after approval's last refusal. A claim is released only by approving its run again without the line (e.g. reopen → reverse the journal → directive cancelled → recalculate → approve); a run reopened and never re-approved keeps it, and nothing deletes a run. A leaver from an earlier period whose approved directive is not paid — unpayable figures (`SEVERANCE_DIRECTIVE_UNPAYABLE`), or severance already paid by hand as a 3901 in a run that has paid (`findHandMadeLumpSumPaid`, P4's `runHasPaid`) — has no line, so the reason is a non-blocking approval-preview advisory `severance_directive_not_paid` (`unpaidLeaverDirectiveNotes`), repeated on every run until the directive is corrected or paid, plus a `log.warn`. The repetition is deliberate (Hein 2026-10-22, G6 won't-fix): do not suppress it. Codes are classified after `normaliseSarsCode` (ASCII space/tab/CR/LF only), the same rule in JS and SQL. The severance-only line takes no ETI (`notEmployedInPeriod`: ETI is apportioned by hours employed, ETI guide Issue 5 §5.3). e@syFile also splits 3605 out of 3601 (`listRunAnnualPayments`). Lock order: approval lock → header → journal chain → directive rows (FOR SHARE) → payment row. Calculation takes no directive row; it only deletes stand-alone payment rows whose journal chain is undone (`releaseReversedStandalonePayment`) and holds nothing an approval needs after that. IRP5 data `lumpSums` and e@syFile 3901/4115 + 3230–3233 (`payrollLumpSumFiling.ts`); 3601 excludes them. Tests: `tests/integration/p3-*.int.test.ts`, `tests/unit/services/payroll/payrollCalculatorAnnualPayment.test.ts`.
- SDL leviability is an EMPLOYER test, not a per-line one: section 4(b) exempts total remuneration <= R500 000 over twelve months. `estimateAnnualRemuneration` bases it on the company's own trailing twelve periods (the eleven `calculated|approved|paid` runs before this one plus this run) using GROSS pay, divided by ELAPSED CALENDAR MONTHS since the company's first run, capped at 12, and by 1 when the window holds no prior run at all — so a seasonal employer's unpaid months count as zero, a company younger than a year extrapolates, and a dormant company resuming payroll is not spread over twelve months it did not pay; the 1% is then charged per line on `sdlLeviable` only. Never gate on the leviable subset — one component flagged `is_sdl_applicable = false` would exempt the whole employer.
- `calculatePayrollLine` takes `annualPayrollEstimate: number | 'defer'`; a run passes `'defer'` and sets `sdl` itself in the second pass.
- **Once-off components close at month end.** `getEmployeeComponents` (the reader `calculatePayrollRun` uses) filters on the `effective_from`/`effective_to` window and IGNORES `is_recurring`, so an open-ended row flagged once-off is paid in every later run. All three writers to `payroll_employee_components` — `postBatch`, `assignComponentToEmployee`, `applyPackageToEmployee` — therefore set `effective_to` to the end of the row's own `effective_from` month when the row is not recurring, via the pure `endOfMonthIso(year, month)` from `leaveAccrualService`. A caller-supplied `effective_to` always wins. Do NOT close at the batch/package period end instead: that bounds only the tail, so a backdated line still pays every month up to it (2026-09-09, K-025).
- `applyPackageToEmployee` supersedes every assignment the apply OVERLAPS (`effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to >= effectiveFrom`), not only open-ended ones — once-off rows are inserted already closed, and an `IS NULL` predicate stepped over them, so re-applying a package in one month paid the once-off twice. A row starting on or after the apply date is voided (empty window) and the service warns naming it, because that silently cancels a future-dated assignment (2026-09-09, K-025).
- Month-end must be derived with UTC accessors. `new Date(y, m + 1, 0).toISOString()` lands a day early east of UTC; `endOfMonthIso` uses `Date.UTC` (2026-09-09, K-025).

- **Cumulative (run-to-date) PAYE (PAYE 4a follow-ups G4) — a business decision, not a SARS prescription (Hein 2026-10-22).** SARS prescribes per-period tables for a full-year employee; G21 2027 p. 8's annual-equivalent formula is for a tax period shorter than a year, and G01 p. 5 accepts programs that "render the same results" — this does not when pay changes (it spreads the change, so can under-deduct that month; employer's risk, accepted). `payeCumulative.ts`: AE = periodic taxable to date × 12 ÷ periods with periodic pay; liability to date = tax(AE) × n/12 + [tax(AE + all annual payments to date) − tax(AE)]; PAYE now = liability − table PAYE already deducted, floored at nil and carried (no in-year refund); the annual-payment part = tax(AE + earlier + this) − tax(AE + earlier) (earlier 3605s stay in the base; G21 p. 32–33). Rebates/credits pro-rated by n/12. Unchanged pay (and any first period) = the ×12 result. A period with neither periodic pay nor an annual payment (severance-only line) deducts nil from the tables. Year-to-date: `payrollYearToDate.loadPayeYearToDate` — the employee's lines on approved/paid runs of the same tax year BEFORE this period (a reopened run, the run itself and later periods are out), directive PAYE excluded; each line stores `periodic_taxable`/`annual_taxable` (mig 913), a line from before 913 is split from its breakdown (taxable 3605 items). A month's PAYE depends on which earlier months are approved when it is calculated; the next month trues it up. A run calculated while LATER months of its tax year are approved (back-fill, or a reopened earlier month) is not refused: its taxed lines carry `PAYE_LATER_PERIODS_APPROVED` (`laterPeriodsWarnings`), since those later months missed it and, if February is among them, nothing trues it up. And a run is refused at approval exactly when its PAYE missed an earlier month, or a later month missed it and, for an employee both pay from the tables (periodic/annual taxable > 0), its line lacks that warning for that month (read off the lines per employee and month, as `laterPeriodsWarnings` writes it: jsonb containment on the warning's `periods` (YYYY-MM), never the message; a warning without `periods`, from #786 dev/test lines, reads as none: refused until recalculated) (`paye_year_to_date_stale`, `payrollYearToDateGate.judgeYearToDate` in the gate, under the company approval lock): recalculate it. Also refused (remedy: the LATER month — reopen it, approve this run, recalculate and approve it): a later month calculated from an EARLIER version of this run (this run approved then, per `approval_history`, its lines rewritten since) that pays someone from the tables whom an earlier approved version taxed (`approved_taxed_employees` UUID[], mig 925: the union over every closed approval, written by `reopenPayrollRun`; NULL with a history = reopened before the column, unknown, conservative, kept NULL) and this run no longer pays from the tables; the union is conservative for someone taxed only in a version that month did not read. A PAID later month is not refused for (it cannot be reopened): named limit (f), with an advisory. The remedy reverses the later month's journal only if its figures change (approval says so). Named limits: (b) the gate ignores how PAYE was computed — a run calculated before cumulative PAYE (lines without `periodic_taxable`) is judged like any other (refused if an earlier month was approved after it; otherwise approved with its ×12 PAYE, which the next month trues up, not February); (a) a NULL `approved_at` (pre-718) counts as approved all along, and a run that missed one is pre-913 too; (c) once the warning names a later month, the gate passes even if that month read this run's EARLIER figures for an employee still taxed here; (d) only approved months are judged: a month reopened and left (or cancelled) is in no pair until approved again; (e) callers with no outer transaction; (f) a PAID later month (legacy rows) keeps this run's old figures, said in the non-blocking preview advisory `paye_paid_later_month_stale`. The one-sentence rule and its completeness argument head `judgeYearToDateStale` (tests: `p4fu-r2-brk-employee-set`, `p4fu-r2-older-version`, `p4fu-r2-brk2-older-version`). "Missed" = the other month, as it now stands (lines no newer), was not approved when this one was calculated (first line's `created_at`); "approved at t" = current `approved_at` ≤ t, or t inside an approval a reopen ended (`approval_history` tstzmultirange, `[approved_at, reopened_at)`, mig 925; `reopenPayrollRun` writes it and `reopened_at` from one `clock_timestamp()`). The whole history, not the last reopen: two reopens leave a gap before the last one (p4fu-r2-exact-gate case 1). Runs reopened before 925 have no history → conservative refusal. All compared times are `clock_timestamp()`. Approve, calculate AND reopen take `lockCompanyPayrollApprovals` before their header lock, so nothing changes declarability between a calculation's year-to-date read and its first line; approvals, reopens and other calculations of the company wait (5 s bound). Kept company-wide, not per tax year (R2): 200-employee calculation p50 147–184 ms, max 233 ms at load ~38 (2026-10-23). Lock order: top of `payrollRunLock.ts`. ETI, UIF, SDL untouched. Tests: `payeCumulative.test.ts`, `tests/integration/p4fu-cumulative-paye.int.test.ts`.
- **Directive filing and integrity (PAYE 4a follow-ups, 2026-10-22).** A directive paid OUTSIDE payroll (`applyTaxDirective`) is declared by `directivePaymentFiling.ts`: EMP201 of its posted journal's month (`directivePayments`, in the totals; the route strips the breakdown for non-payroll-detail roles), and the certificate for that tax year (`listCertificateLumpSums` unions run and stand-alone; mig 901's CHECK keeps them disjoint). Only while its journal is in force (`payrollJournalInForce`). Codes: severance/retirement/death 3901 with PAYE in 4115; lump_sum 3907 with PAYE in 4102 (`lumpSumPayeCode`; G21 2027 p. 15, 21–22; BRS V25.3.0 p. 57). Apply refuses a directive not linked to a payroll employee (400) or not approved (409), and takes the directive row FOR SHARE. A certificate with no tax is an IT3(a) with 4150 = 04 (directive) or 02 (`buildEmployeeRecord`; `validateCertificateTaxFields` in `irp5ValidationEngine.ts` enforces the BRS 3015/4115/4150 rules). 3231 = `tax_directives.issued_date` (mig 912), else effective date with a warning (`X-IsaFlow-Warnings` on the e@syFile export, shown on the IRP5 page). A directive whose payment stands cannot leave `approved` (`updateTaxDirective` + `taxDirectivePaidGuard.ts`, 409; reverse the booking journal first); lock order there. The UI lump-sum calculator uses the SARS 2027 table (`src/lib/taxCalculations.ts`, `LUMP_SUM_TAX_YEAR`). Tests: `tests/integration/p3fu-*.int.test.ts`, `easyFileCertificateTax`, `lumpSumTaxTable2027`.

- **Medical credits: record, certificate, 65+ credit (PAYE 4a follow-ups round 2, R3, mig 926; Hein 2026-10-23).** Each run line stores `medical_credit` (4116), `additional_medical_credit` (4120) and `medical_scheme_fees` (deductions coded 4005, the calculator's `medicalSchemeFees`; employer-paid medical aid, a 3810 benefit, is not supported). A credit record = the credit inside the line's PAYE liability to date less what the employee's earlier lines of the tax year recorded (`payeCumulative`: used(x) from `annualTaxAfterCredits` `medicalCreditUsed` / `additionalMedicalCreditUsed`, weighted used(AE) × n ÷ 12 + [used(AE + A) − used(AE)]; `loadPayeYearToDate` sums the records). So a year's lines add up to the credit inside its liability; a line after pre-926 lines (NULL) carries their credit; a credit the liability no longer holds is a negative record; a severance-only line records nil. **65+ additional credit in PAYE** (`payeEngine.computeAdditionalMedicalCredit`): 65 or older on the year's last day, 33,3% × (annual 4005 fees − 3 × annual MTC), after the MTC, non-refundable (s6B(3)(a)(i), Fourth Schedule para 9(6); SARS Guide on the Determination of Medical Tax Credits, Issue 18, p. 21, 31-32; out-of-pocket expenses are excluded by the guide and not held). Cumulatively the fees to date are annualised over the pay's n (`loadMedicalRecord` reads them, a pre-926 line from its breakdown), so the credit to date is 33,3% × (F − 3 × MTC × n ÷ 12); the first month after earlier months without it takes the whole credit to date (floored at nil, carried). PAYE changes ONLY for 65+ with fees above 3 × MTC (golden grid `payeMedicalCreditIdentity.test.ts`, real-PG golden `p4fu-r2b-amtc-identity`). **Certificate** (`easyFileMedicalFields.ts`, `payrollMedicalRecord.ts`): 4005 (cents dropped), 4116 and, for 65+, 4120 only beside a 4005 value and only when the latest taxed month carries the record (else left off, `X-IsaFlow-Warnings`); a nil-tax certificate above the threshold is an IT3(a) with 4150 = 08 when a reported credit is above nil, else refused naming the missing 4005; `validateCertificateTaxFields` enforces BRS V25.3.0 p. 59-61 (`medicalFieldRules`, incl. 4120 against the age from 3080, else the ID number 3060). **Supported medical aid setup (round 2 review):** the employee's FULL scheme contribution is a deduction component coded 4005; an employer share is a separate taxable earning (IsaFlow has no 3810 fringe-benefit handling, and `component_type` VARCHAR(20) cannot even hold 'employer_contribution'). Employer-paid or privately paid medical aid with no 4005 deduction gets the MTC in PAYE but no 4005/4116 on the IRP5 and no 65+ credit; the export warns (`medicalCertificateWarnings`), as it does for a 65+ employee (by ID number) with no date of birth (PAYE's age reads the date of birth only; not changed, a PAYE change). The 65+ credit needs scheme membership on the employee (beneficiaries > 0). `calculatePAYE.medicalCreditsApplied` stays the s6A credit only. Tests: `payeMedicalCredit`, `payeAdditionalMedicalCredit`, `easyFileMedicalCertificate`, `tests/integration/p4fu-r2b-{medical-credit,medical-certificate,amtc-identity}.int.test.ts`.

- 2026-10-01 (W3-01 round 5, adversarial round on 25170a6fd): **a pay run's journal is judged by the LEDGER, not by `reversed_at`.** `payrollJournalChain.ts` reads the linked journal's whole reversal chain (journal → its reversal → a reversal of that → …) and nets its posted lines: `in_force` (nets to the journal; a lone posted journal always is), `out` (nets to zero), `unclear` (a draft in the chain, or no mirror). Three callers, one judgement: the approval gate (`in_force` → re-lock while figures match; `out` → `replaces`, a fresh journal; `unclear` → `posted_journal_not_live`, naming the journals), `calculatePayrollRun`'s loan guard (`journalInForceOrNull` — a run with loan work recalculates once its journal is out), and the generic reversal.
  - **`reverseJournalEntry` is payroll-aware** (`payrollJournalReversalGuard.ts`, called from the GL service, so the HTTP route, MCP `reverse_journal_entry` — whose dry run asks the same question read-only — and every service caller are covered). Scope: a pay RUN's journal (source `auto_payroll` and linked by a run, or described `Payroll run YYYY-MM`); UIF and tax-directive payments are not. Refused: reversing the last journal of a chain that nets to zero (it would re-book the run beside a later journal — approve the run again instead), and reversing the in-force journal of an `approved` or `paid` run (reopen first; a paid run cannot be). `reversePayrollRunJournal` goes through the same guard, so it too needs the run reopened.
  - **LOCK ORDER: run header → the run's journal (chain root) → each reversal in chain order.** Approval takes them before its gate reads; the reversal guard takes the same, in the same order, before `claimJournalReversal` (which locks only the entry being reversed — always the end of a chain). All waits are 5s. `reopenPayrollRun` takes the header lock too.
  - **Recalculated since posting → labour is compared PER ACCOUNT** (`runRecalculatedSince`: the run lines' `created_at`, stamped with `clock_timestamp()` at the insert, against the header's `lines_confirmed_at` — see the round 6–7 entries; the journal's `created_at` only for a run approved before migration 718). A recalculation can swap pay between cost centres and leave every header total alone; the split is then a real figure on a real expense account. A never-recalculated run keeps the totals-only rule (cost-centre/mapping/allocation changes and the old rounding cent are not the run changing).
  - **ACCOUNTING RULING NEEDED — the date of a replacement journal.** Implemented as recommended, pending Hein's decision (`payrollApprovalGate#datedForReplacement`): when the reversal that took the old journal out is not in the run's month (the month was closed, so the reversal was dated later), the replacement is dated ON THE REVERSAL'S DATE. Reversal and replacement net in one period; the run's month keeps the figures it reported; the later month carries only the correction. The preview says so (`replacement_dated_on_reversal` advisory, `plan.entryDate`) and the hash covers it. THE ALTERNATIVE: date the replacement in the run's own month — which needs that period reopened AND the reversal moved into it, or the month carries the run twice and the later month a negative (what round 4 did). Not implemented.
  - **Every chain walk is bounded** (`MAX_CHAIN_JOURNALS` = 25: both recursive reads carry a depth cap, the lock walk locks a row once and stops at the cap). Reversal links that loop (A reversed by B and B by A, a journal reversing itself) or run past the cap make the chain `broken`: the gate answers `posted_journal_not_live`, the reversal guard refuses, the loan guard treats the journal as in force. Tests: `tests/unit/services/payroll/payrollJournalChainLock.test.ts`, `tests/integration/w3-01-forged-reversal-links.int.test.ts`.
  - `planHash` now covers run id, entry date and description (two months with equal figures shared a hash). The two scripts that call calculate/approve directly run them in `withAlsTransaction`, so the header lock holds.
  - Known, not fixed here: `POST /api/payroll/runs` has no `withWriteAccess` (a viewer can create a run); the GL's entry-number race (`uq_gl_je_company_entry_number`) still turns one of two simultaneous postings into a 500 that rolls back.
  - Tests: `tests/integration/brkr-c1…c7*.int.test.ts` (the adversarial repros, ported), `w3-01-reversed-journal-reapprove`, `w3-01-approve-approve-race`, `w3-01-calculate-approve-race`.
- 2026-10-01 (W3-01 round 4): `approvePayrollRun` takes the header lock through `lockPayrollRunHeader` too (5s; `PayrollLoanLockTimeoutError` → route 503 + Retry-After with `code` (D11; was 400), MCP tool error), then `lockRunJournalForApproval` locks the linked journal and its reversal before the gate reads them. **Lock order: run header → linked journal → its reversal.** `reverseJournalEntry` locks only the one entry it reverses and never the run header, so no inversion; a reversal that arrives while approval decides waits until it commits. `calculatePayrollRun`'s final header UPDATE moved to `saveCalculatedRunTotals` (`payrollRunLock.ts`), still predicated on an unlocked status — the only protection for callers with no transaction open (scripts). `reopenPayrollRun` throws `PayrollRunReopenRefusedError` for its refusals; the route answers only that as 400 and rethrows the rest (500, rollback). `calculate` and `reopen` validate the run id as a UUID (400). Tests: `tests/integration/w3-01-approve-approve-race.int.test.ts`, `w3-01-calculate-lock-timeout.int.test.ts`, `w3-01-calculate-approve-race.int.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api/payrollReopenRoute.test.ts`, `payrollCalculateRefusals.test.ts`.

A reversal that was itself reversed has re-booked the amounts and stays `posted_journal_not_live`; so does a draft or missing journal. Before this the month was a dead end (`reverse the posted journal first` → reversed → refused for ever; a new run is a duplicate). **B/C** `recalculated_after_posting` compares `figures`: each credit account and the labour debit as ONE total — never the cost-centre split, which follows today's centres/mappings/allocations and, before round 2's `ORDER BY`, heap order for its rounding cent. **D** `postPayrollRunJournal(…, { plan })` posts the plan the gate judged; `approvePayrollRun` no longer lets it rebuild one. `reopenPayrollRun`'s UPDATE is predicated on `status = 'approved'`. `findApprovalBlocker` is gone (the MCP dry run reads `previewPayrollApproval`). - 2026-09-09: `calculatePayrollRun` reverses the loan payments it previously applied before re-applying them (K-022). Without it a second calculation found every schedule row `paid_flag = true`, injected no LOAN deduction, and left `outstanding_balance` reduced for a repayment the payslip no longer took. The pair runs in one `withTransaction` under `FOR UPDATE` on the affected loans; `applyLoanToRun` / `listActiveLoansForRun` take an optional `TxSql` executor so they join it. A run reopened with `journal_entry_id` still set is refused whether it would undo an old instalment or take a new one — `reopenPayrollRun` does NOT reverse the GL entry, so recalculating would move the subledger under a journal that `postPayrollRunJournal` will not re-post. `PayrollRunJournalPostedError` is mapped to a 400 and `PayrollLoanLockTimeoutError` (a held run row) to a 503 + Retry-After (D11) in `pages/api/payroll/runs/[id]/calculate.ts` and to a tool error in `calculate_pay_run`; unmapped they reach the caller as a 500 and their instructions are lost.

The restore MUST be relative: assigning `loan_balance_before` absolutely erases a later period's instalment from the balance while its payment row still records it. `calculate_pay_run`'s `dry_run` and the live path both read the guard through `readRunLoanWork`, so the dry run cannot promise a recost that would be refused; never write that condition out a second time. `payroll_loan_payment_reversals.stranded` marks a tombstone written while reclaiming a payment whose own run was deleted.
